page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard2.4 is a compute instance within the Standard family, designed to balance processing throughput and memory capacity. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8167M processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The instance allocates 4 physical CPU cores configured with 2 threads per core, yielding 8 dedicated vCPUs. CPU allocation is fully dedicated rather than shared or burstable, ensuring steady processing capacity without resource contention from neighboring tenants.

The instance includes 60.0 GB of system memory, which translates to 7.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. This elevated memory density positions the shape between standard balanced ratios and memory-centric offerings. VM.Standard2.4 contains no bundled local storage, requiring persistent workloads to utilize remote block volumes or network-attached file systems for operating system and data disks. Additionally, the instance provides 1 complimentary public IPv4 address for external network routing and contains no GPU accelerators.

Operationally, the absence of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators means performance depends on external network storage latency and CPU-bound execution. The dedicated thread model combined with 60 GB of memory makes VM.Standard2.4 well configured for memory-dependent applications, mid-sized relational database deployments, enterprise application runtimes, data parsing pipelines, and distributed caching nodes.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard2.4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration engineered for enterprise applications requiring balanced compute and memory capacity. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates an Intel Xeon 8167M processor running at 2.0 GHz, delivering 4 physical cores configured across 8 dedicated vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading. It features 60 GB of system memory, providing 7.5 GB of RAM per vCPU, which supports higher-memory working sets than conventional cloud instances. The VM.Standard2.4 instance does not include integrated local disk storage, depending on remote block storage solutions for persistent data, and does not feature GPU acceleration. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned by default. Due to its dedicated CPU threads and substantial memory allocation per core, this instance type fits workloads such as relational database hosting, backend enterprise application servers, in-memory caching solutions, and general batch processing pipelines.
